Bug_Details:
Marking an array volatile means that the array itself will always be read fresh and never thread cached, but the items in the
array will not be. Similarly, marking a mutable object field volatile means the object reference is volatile but
the object itself is not, and other threads may not see updates to the object state.
This can be salvaged with arrays by using the relevant AtomicArray class, such as AtomicIntegerArray , instead. For mutable objects,
the volatile should be removed, and some other method should be used to ensure thread-safety, such as synchronization, or ThreadLocal
storage.
Noncompliant code example
private volatile int [] vInts;  // Noncompliant
private volatile MyObj myObj;  // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
private AtomicIntegerArray vInts;
private MyObj myObj;
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by marking a non-primitive array 'vInts' and a non-primitive object'myObj' as volatile. This does not ensure that changes to the array elements or object fields are visible to other threads.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases call methods'showBug1' and'showBug2' which modify the volatile non-primitive fields 'vInts' and'myObj'. The tests are designed to fail due to the visibility issues caused by the volatile keyword on non-primitive types.
